name: Trung Xi Nhat Nham
role: Interpreter on the mountain; Larry says a warrior monk
summary: The man Larry names in VN-0148, standing at the burnt-out helicopter on Núi Bà Đen: "Trung Xi Nhat Nham is whose in the picture. He was protecting me. He was an interpreter and could speak 9 languages. He was a warrior monk." He is the only person Larry has described as protecting him. His son reports that Larry does not know his rank and that he seemed more of a Buddhist than a soldier.
researchNotes: The rendering is his son's transcription of what Larry says, not a spelling Larry gave letter by letter, so it records a sound rather than an orthography. The cold question about his name and rank was asked on 2026-09-03 (data/recollections/2026-09-03-phone-the-interpreter.json, paraphrase): Larry did not separate a rank from the name, and gave a second phonetic rendering. That is not independent confirmation of the reading of the name filed in research/people/trung-xi-nhat-nham.md, which is still not repeated here; the interview guide records that a search may now proceed on it (issue #90). Nine languages is an unusually specific and searchable claim: interpreters of that calibre at a Special Forces site were few, and the combination with a religious vocation is rarer still. Núi Bà Đen was a pilgrimage mountain with an active temple complex on its slopes. As of 2026-09-14 no documentary search has been recorded. 2026-09-15, on his son's decision (no spelling notes on public pages): the rendered aliases were trimmed; removed from display, kept here: "Trang-Zee-Nee-Yot-Na-Yong (his son's rendering of the sound, 2026-09-03)".
